description:
For me, making music, and especially music I’m proud of, doesn’t always come so easily. At least when I think about making music, I worry that I’ve already done all that I can and there’s nothing left for me to say. It starts to put me into a really insecure phase of my life that sometimes lasts long enough for me to be able to convince myself that I’ll never be able to make good music again. 

Then someone like Dux comes back around and says he wants me to write to one of his latest beats for his latest album. My initial thoughts were “hell no! I can’t do this anymore! I’m going to have bad ideas!!” So obviously I said “Sure, I’d love to.” We worked on a song for his album that got me really excited about making music again (In case you’re wondering, that song is called “Over It”). 

Once that song was out, I realized I really wanted Dux to be part of my next album. I shared a few ideas with him and showed him what I had been working on, so he went to work up in Portland and came up with a few beat ideas for me. Then he came down to LA and stayed with us at Blue Dream Studios for a few days while we worked on these ideas, made a lot of food and bonded over our famous Blue Dream cocktails. 

During that time, Back To Me immediately felt like it was craving to be an anthem. That had me thinking a lot about what I wanted the song to be about. Even though the verses didn’t come right away, I knew that the chorus would be repetitive and empowering. I was on a high from all of this new music, good recipes, great hangs, amazing conversations, belly laughs, etc… It made me reminisce on the times I’ve felt happiest in my life and they all have these same common factors, and they’re all things that make me feel like myself. That’s where “I think I’m finally starting to feel like me again, I think I’m finally back to me” came from. Once I started singing that over and over, I realized I needed to write about why I didn’t feel like me for awhile. 

I feel like I’ve made mistakes in my life and I convinced myself that I could never move on from those mistakes without still feeling regretful or feeling like I could have done things differently. But we all make mistakes and there’s no point in trying to change things you can’t change. You just have to learn, grow and go. Eventually, when you make another mistake, own it, accept it and learn to keep moving forward and allowing yourself to be happy.
